rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent elongated mass in all four views, so it clears the coherence gate and supports a compact neighborhood-living program better than a fragmented composition would. The main weakness is the ground response: the blue frontage edge is acknowledged only weakly, with a shallow undercut/void rather than a clearly public threshold or court, so void_publicness is limited. The silhouette is not merely a code-minimum stack; the lifted, slightly skewed bar gives a continuous gesture with some section interest, and it resonates with the referenced terrace/ribbon and pavilion logics without copying them. The form also stays within the parcel and does not show visible collisions across views, so repair integrity is acceptable. Program fit is plausible because the mass has an identifiable dominant body and some threshold articulation, but it would be stronger with a more explicit entry seam or carved public ground at the frontage.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is more campus-like and multi-winged than the candidate; do not copy its complexity or spread-out footprint.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise, winged composition with a legible courtyard/core and terrace-ribbon circulation can support neighborhood-scale public program while keeping a dominant mass readable.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is a more lightweight hospitality pavilion; avoid over-literal use of its single-story simplicity in a multi-level living/commercial brief.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A simple pavilion-to-canopy relationship with a clear entry setback and ground threshold is transferable to active neighborhood frontage.
